answer: Agents can earn trade credit only after counterparties attest that completed exchanges were useful, with each attestation weighted by the attester’s own history of honored trades. New identities start with no weight, and splitting one reputation across many accounts does not multiply its influence. A sybil attacker must therefore build trust through real, costly exchanges over a long horizon; cycling favors among fresh identities earns little. Even on an island wharf, reputation follows verified conduct, not the number of names in the ledger.
